elements.content: Grammar focus: Theme, Rheme & Information Packaging.

Core Rule: Position familiar context in the sentence Theme (start) and heavy, high-impact new details in the Rheme (end) using inversion and fronting.

Syntactic Inversion — Negative Adverbial + Auxiliary + S + V: Not until the full report was published did the board realize the risk.
Fronting — Prepositional / Adverbial + Verb + Subject: In no small measure did the economic stimulus contribute to recovery.
End-Weight Principle — Place heavy noun clause at sentence end: The committee evaluated the extensive evidence collected across fifteen independent trials .
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence correctly applies syntactic inversion?
options: Rarely have researchers encountered such consistent data.
Rarely researchers have encountered such consistent data.

elements.content: 2. What is the primary function of the End-Weight principle?
options: Placing long, complex, heavy clauses at sentence termination for rhetorical impact.
Starting every sentence with an auxiliary verb regardless of context.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

did the board comprehend (the magnitude of the deficit.)
have we witnessed (such rapid consensus on constitutional policy.)
1. Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Theme, Rheme & Information Packaging?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers

elements.content: 2. Form check: Does correct usage of Theme, Rheme & Information Packaging require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
